Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

problem noun

a difficulty

also no problem, what’s the problem?, difficulty, difficulties, trouble (difficulties), challenge (a hard task)

classical

Cic. Att. 8.3.5: in utrāque enim rē summa difficultās erit
M-O s.v. problem

difficultās, difficultātis f.

noun, third declension

a difficulty, a problem

Other words

  • negōtium, negōtiī n. — trouble, bother: quid est negōtī?, what’s the problem?

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Most. 741: sed quid est negōtī?; Cic. Att. 10.16.3: nūllō negōtiō, without any trouble; Traupman 91, 106, 364

    Properly “business”; in comedy and in Cicero also “trouble”.

  • incommodum, incommodī n. — a drawback, an inconvenience, something that goes wrong

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.102: plūs habeat adjūmentī quam incommodī; M-O s.v. problem

  • molestia, molestiae f. — trouble, bother, annoyance

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 4.18: molestia aegritūdō permanēns, a lasting distress

  • problēma, problēmatis n. — a puzzle set for solving, not a difficulty

    noun, third declension · avoid · classical · Suet. Gram. 4; Gell. 19.4.1 (Lewis & Short)

    Lewis & Short: “a question proposed for solution, a problem, enigma, riddle”. For a difficulty that troubles you, use difficultās or negōtium; for a puzzle, see problem (to be solved).

Examples

  • negōtium magnum est nāvigāre atque id mēnse Quīntīlī

    sailing is a big problem, and in July at thatCic. Att. 5.12.1

  • est magnum illud quidem vērum tamen multiplex puerī ingenium; quō ego regendō habeō negōtī satis

    the boy has a great nature, but a complicated one, and steering it gives me trouble enoughCic. Att. 6.2.2

  • in hāc causā mihi aqua haeret

    in this matter I’m stuck (literally, the water-clock stops for me)Cic. Q. fr. 2.6.1

See also problem, what’s the matter?, stuck, solution, trouble, trouble.
